title: Next Greater Element I
statement: `nums1` is a subset of `nums2`. For each value in nums1, find the next greater element in nums2 to its right. If none exists, use -1. Return the answers in the order of nums1.
hints: Compute the next greater element for every index of nums2 first.
A decreasing stack resolves next-greater as soon as a larger value arrives.
Store the result in a map from value to next greater, then read it for nums1.

approaches.name: Scan nums2 for each query
approaches.explanation: Find the value, then scan right.

approaches.name: Monotonic stack plus map
approaches.explanation: One pass over nums2 answers every value.

editorial: Walk nums2 with a decreasing stack of values. When nums2[i] is larger than the top, it is the next greater element of every popped value. Unpopped values map to -1. Query the map for each element of nums1.

examples.explanation: None of 4, 1's next is 3, and 2 has none. Wait: 4 has none, 1 maps to 3, 2 has none.
